title: Biological growth, asbestos and unexpected hazards
audience: Trainees and workers on the roof soft washing track, and supervisors who decide what happens when an unexpected hazard appears on a roof. Asbestos removal is not part of this course.
learningOutcomes: Recognise biological growth on a roof and explain why it can hide the condition of the material beneath.
Identify roof sheeting that may contain asbestos and apply a do-not-disturb and refer decision.
Apply a stop-work and referral decision to an unexpected roof hazard, such as structural damage, nests or a mould-affected roof space.

instruction.heading: Biological growth on roofs
instruction.body: Moss, lichen, algae and fungal staining are common on roofs in many climates. They can look like ordinary dirt, but they can also hold moisture against the sheeting, hide cracks and loose fixings, and make surfaces slippery. Soft washing is intended for surfaces of this kind, but the growth is also a sign that the roof may have a moisture or ventilation problem. Record the extent of the growth, its position, and any sign of damage beneath it. Do not record that the growth has been removed or that the surface is sound, unless a competent person has confirmed it.

instruction.heading: Asbestos in roof sheeting
instruction.body: Older roof sheeting, especially fibre cement sheeting, may contain asbestos. A WA Department of Health guidance note dates widespread use of asbestos cement roofing from the 1930s to roughly 1987, and treats 1990 as the boundary for presuming a material may be asbestos. Washing, scraping, cutting or walking on such sheeting can break it and release fibres. Queensland's asbestos guidance says material should be assumed to be asbestos-containing if no sample analysis has been done. Victoria's WorkSafe warns tradies to check pre-1990 buildings for asbestos before starting work, because breaking such materials can free fibres into the air. The Safe Work Australia model code on managing asbestos is listed for its title and model status only, and whether it applies depends on each state. Removal licence rules differ by state. Each state's official source, checked on 3 November 2026, says the following. New South Wales: a friable asbestos removal licence is needed to remove any amount of friable asbestos, and a non-friable licence is needed to remove more than 10 square metres of non-friable asbestos. Victoria: removal must be done by a licence holder, and the only unlicensed exception on the page is non-friable asbestos of 10 square metres or less that takes no more than 1 hour in any 7-day period, counted across all employees. Friable asbestos has no such allowance, and work above these limits needs a licence. South Australia: a Class A licence is needed to remove friable asbestos, and a Class A licence also covers removal of non-friable asbestos; a Class B licence is needed for more than 10 square metres of non-friable asbestos (source: the SafeWork SA applicant guide, Asbestos removal licence guide for applicants, page date not shown; the main licence page could not be retrieved). Western Australia: a licence is needed to remove asbestos; Class A covers friable asbestos of any amount, and Class B covers more than 10 square metres of non-friable asbestos. Tasmania: a licence is needed for any amount of friable asbestos and for more than 10 square metres of non-friable asbestos; below that non-friable threshold the code of practice still applies. Northern Territory: a Class A licence covers any amount of friable asbestos, and a Class B licence covers more than 10 square metres of non-friable asbestos. Australian Capital Territory: only a Class A licence holder may remove friable asbestos, a Class A licence holder may also remove non-friable asbestos, a Class B licence holder may remove non-friable asbestos, and the page gives no size threshold. Queensland: the page says to assume material is asbestos-containing if no sample analysis has been done, and it does not state a removal licence rule for roof sheeting. None of the removal licence pages checked names roof sheeting as its own category. If the age or material of the roof sheeting is unknown, treat it as possibly containing asbestos, stop, and refer it to a competent person before any washing, scraping or walking on it.

instruction.heading: Do not disturb: what to do
instruction.body: If suspect sheeting is found, do not pressure wash it, scrape it, drill it, cut it or walk on it. The WA guidance describes high-pressure cleaning of this sheeting as hazardous and unlawful, because it can spread contaminated sludge (guidance note, copyright 2016; no publication date shown). Keep people and animals clear of the area below, and cover or isolate any drainage where it could carry debris. Record the location, the material's appearance, its age if known, and the people told. Tell the owner and the site controller in writing, and do not continue the wash on that section. Removal, encapsulation and clearance of asbestos are specialist tasks that this course does not cover.

instruction.heading: Structural damage and unexpected conditions
instruction.body: A roof may show rotten timber, loose or lifted sheeting, corroded fixings, sagging, cracked battens or a damaged gutter bracket. These are conditions that change the fall risk and the load on the roof. A worker does not decide whether the structure is safe. Stop, keep the area clear, record the condition, and refer it to a competent person. The worker also does not certify or warrant that the roof is structurally sound after the job.

instruction.heading: Nests, animals and biological hazards
instruction.body: Birds, bats, wasps and other animals may nest in roof voids, gutters or under sheeting. Some nests carry risks such as stings, droppings and bacteria. Check for nests before access, and do not disturb an active nest. Check the rule for the state before any removal. Keep the work area clear of animals and record the presence of nests so that the owner can decide on removal through the proper channel.

instruction.heading: Mould in roof spaces
instruction.body: Roof voids can contain mould, particularly where there has been water entry or poor ventilation. Soft washing of a roof surface does not treat mould in the void or the framing, and a surface wash does not provide a clearance. Where mould is visible in a roof void, a loft, a roof space or on framing, stop the work in that area and refer it to a competent person. Mould remediation is covered in the high-risk cleaning module of this curriculum, and that module is not a routine soft washing method.

instruction.heading: Licence and authority boundary
instruction.body: Licence notice: This lesson does not grant a licence, certificate, asbestos authority, roof-work authority or clearance. State removal licence rules are set out above, but none of the pages checked names roof sheeting as its own category, so check with the relevant regulator before relying on this point for roof sheeting. The lesson does not describe a removal route and does not authorise any worker to disturb suspect material.

procedure: Record the extent, position and appearance of any biological growth, and note any sign of damage or moisture beneath it.
Check the roof sheeting for age and material where known, and treat unknown sheeting as possibly containing asbestos.
If suspect sheeting is found, stop, do not pressure wash, scrape, cut or walk on it, and keep people clear below.
Check for active nests and animals before access, and do not disturb an active nest.
Stop and refer any structural damage, loose or lifted sheeting, or corroded fixings to a competent person.
Stop in any roof space where mould is visible, and refer it to a competent person.
Tell the owner and the site controller in writing about each hazard, and record the people told.
Do not resume work on a section until the hazard is cleared by a competent person or the scope is re-approved.

workedExamples.situation: Halfway through a soft wash, a worker finds that the sheeting on the rear plane is grey and brittle, and the owner says it was installed in the 1970s.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must the worker do, and what can the business tell the owner?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop work on that plane. The age of the sheeting suggests it may contain asbestos, so do not pressure wash, scrape or walk on it. Keep people clear below, and record the location and the appearance. Tell the owner in writing that the section has been held pending identification by a competent person. The business must not state that the sheeting is safe to wash, and removal is outside this course.

workedExamples.situation: A worker sees dark growth in the roof space through an access hatch, with a musty smell and staining on the timber framing.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is a surface soft wash of the roof enough to deal with this?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The growth is in the roof void, on the framing. A surface soft wash does not treat it, and it does not provide a clearance. Stop work in the roof space, record what was seen and smelled, and refer it to a competent person. The owner should be told that the surface wash does not address the void.

equipmentAndPpe: Photographs and a sketch of the roof plane with the position of growth and suspect sheeting
Hold notice and referral template for asbestos and mould concerns
Access hatch inspection checklist with a no-entry rule for the roof space
Respiratory and PPE protection only as directed by the competent person; no disturbance of suspect material

commonErrors.error: Pressure washing old fibre cement sheeting to clean it.
commonErrors.prevention: Treat old or unknown sheeting as possibly containing asbestos, and do not wash, scrape or walk on it.

commonErrors.error: Telling an owner that growth has been removed and the roof is sound.
commonErrors.prevention: Record only what was observed, and refer structural and integrity questions.

commonErrors.error: Treating mould in a roof void as a surface wash.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop in the roof space and refer it to a competent person.

commonErrors.error: Disturbing an active nest to clear the gutter.
commonErrors.prevention: Check for nests before access and refer active nests for a proper removal route.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Asbestos: removal licence rules are set state by state, as summarised in this lesson. Safe Work Australia's model asbestos code is a model only, and its legal effect depends on the regulator (no date shown). The WA Department of Health and Queensland guidance cited here treat unsampled or older sheeting as possibly asbestos-containing, but none of the removal licence pages checked names roof sheeting as its own category, so check the requirements for identifying and handling roof sheeting with the regulator.

Falls: fragile sheeting, skylights and voids are fall hazards. SafeWork NSW's construction guidance orders the control options, from ground-level or solid-structure working down to fall arrest (no date shown).
Mould: surface soft washing does not treat mould in roof voids. Mould remediation is covered by the high-risk cleaning module of this curriculum.
Licence notice: This lesson does not grant a licence, certificate, asbestos authority, clearance or roof-work authority.

qualityStandard: Suspect sheeting is not disturbed, and the section is held and referred.
Biological growth and structural conditions are recorded as observations, not findings of safety.
Mould in a roof void is referred and not treated by a surface wash.
Owner and site controller are told in writing about each hazard.
documentationEvidence: Record of growth extent, position and any sign of damage beneath it
Sheeting age and material where known, with the decision for unknown sheeting
Hold and referral record for asbestos, structural or mould concerns, with the person notified
Record of nests or animals found before access
summary: Biological growth can hide damage and moisture, so record it as an observation.
Treat old or unknown roof sheeting as possibly containing asbestos, and do not disturb it.
Stop and refer structural damage, nests and mould in roof voids.
This lesson grants no asbestos authority, clearance, roof-work authority or licence.

knowledgeChecks.question: Grey, brittle fibre cement sheeting from an older building is found on the roof. What is the correct first action?
options: Pressure wash it on a low setting, since the sheeting can take a light wash safely
Scrape it to see what it is made of underneath the surface layer and the coat
Stop, do not wash, scrape or walk on it, and refer it as possibly containing asbestos
Walk on it carefully to inspect the fixings and the sheet edges along the whole ridge line

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does a surface soft wash not treat visible mould in a roof void?
options: Because soft washing kills mould on contact, so the void is cleaned too on the day of the wash
Because mould is only found on roof tiles and never in the void space under the roof sheeting itself
Because the customer has not paid for the void work in full yet, so it is left out until payment clears
Because the void is not part of the surface and a surface wash does not treat it or give a clearance

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the correct response to an active bird nest in the gutter before access?
options: Check for it, and refer it for a proper removal route rather than disturbing it
Remove it quickly with a hose before the next visit to the roof and the gutter
Ignore it and continue with the wash as planned on the whole roof area today
Burn it off the roof and the gutter with a torch and then clean the area

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement about the roof's structure is within a worker's remit?
options: The roof is structurally sound after the wash is complete and dry today
Rotten timber or lifted sheeting is observed and referred to a competent person
The roof will last ten more years with the wash in place on it every time
The roof has no structural issues that anyone needs to note at all

knowledgeChecks.question: Does this lesson grant an asbestos removal or clearance authority?
options: Yes, for small areas that look clean and safe enough
Yes, once the quiz is passed by the worker today
No, it grants no asbestos authority, clearance or licence
Yes, if the owner agrees to it in writing for the job
